Subject: Production: Rapid 5xx/429 surge + timeouts on /v1/infer — urgent

Ben —

We started seeing a sudden spike in 5xx and 429 responses across our inference calls to your hosted endpoints starting ~08:45 PST. Latencies also spiked; many requests timed out at 15s. The error patterns look like a retry amplification — our clients retried and that multiplied the traffic.

We captured a few request ids and a short error sample (attached). Topline: ~18% 5xx/429 across the fleet for our service, and it’s impacting critical customer flows. We need immediate help — can you confirm whether this is a config issue on our side (batching/payload) or a backend capacity/auto-scale problem on Redwood?

Request ids attached: request-ids-20270114.txt
Attachment: initial-error-sample.txt (text)

Please escalate if needed — we have execs watching.

Thanks,
Maya Rios
SRE, Stellaris Health
maya@stellarishealth.com

Subject: Re: Production: Rapid 5xx/429 surge + timeouts on /v1/infer — urgent

Maya — thanks for the quick heads up and the request ids. I’m looping in our SRE and engineering leads (Markus, Sean) and CS (Laura, Monica) so we can triage immediately.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the approximate QPS to us across the last 30 minutes and any big batch jobs kicked off?
- If you can, send one full raw request payload and the associated request-id from the attachment so Markus can reproduce locally.

We will:
1) Check pool health and autoscaling activity (Markus).
2) If it’s an autoscale lag / GPU exhaustion, we can failover a portion of traffic to a warm Dedicated pool for you while we stabilize.
3) Put short-term throttles and enable lower batch sizes on your route to curb amplification.

I’ve flagged this as high priority. Laura/Monica — we’ll propose a short customer message and a mutual action plan (MAP) to share in the next 20–30m.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: Rapid 5xx/429 surge + timeouts on /v1/infer — urgent

Ben / team — quick summary from infra: we’re seeing rapid node eviction in the shared hosted pool servicing Stellaris routes. Metrics: GPU memory pressure -> OOM kill on a few nodes, autoscaler reacted but with 60–90s lag while instances came online. During that window, queue depth rose and our gate returned 429s, then 5xx downstream as some inference shards hit memory errors.

Attached: pool-metrics-20270114.png (screenshot of GPU memory + autoscale events)

Preliminary mitigation options I recommend immediately:
- Move 40% of Stellaris traffic to a warm Dedicated pool we have available in us-west-2 (we can do this in ~8–12m).
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_size on their route from 32 -> 8 to lower per-request memory.
- Enable prefix/KV caching on their common prompts to reduce compute.
- Add a short 250ms client-side jitter backoff recommendation to reduce synchronized retries.

This is looking like capacity exhaustion during a burst combined with aggressive batching patterns. If they approve Dedicated spillover we’ll avoid another 5–10 minute degradation window while nodes ramp.

-Markus
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Please reply with GO to authorize the spillover and changes.

Customer Success
